_meta.purpose: Governs validator rule R6. Two indexed pages may render the same Arabic only when the cluster appears in `allowed` below with a stated reason and a named adjudicator. Anything else fails the build.
_meta.status: PARTLY ENFORCED. R6 itself is still not implemented in any script; R8 (validate-seo.mjs) enforces the related question of never linking an unpublished page. 4 of the 8 registered clusters were adjudicated by the owner on 2026-08-03 and moved to `allowed`; the rest remain unadjudicated and are NOT permitted.
_meta.normalisationIsPartOfTheRule: R6 compares NORMALISED Arabic, never raw. The seed pair is NOT byte-identical and NOT equal under the corpus's ordinary diacritic strip — it differs only in Uthmani orthography. A rule written on `identical arabic` is a no-op against the exact pair it was created for. See R6 §Normalisation.
_meta.clusteringIsCorpusWide: Clusters are computed across the whole corpus, not across the sitemap, so a pair is registered before either member is ever approved for indexing. R6 then fails only when 2+ members of a cluster are simultaneously indexed.
_meta.adjudicationIsNotClaudeCode's: Deciding whether two occasions genuinely share a text is a sourcing question about what each narration attests. Entries move from `pendingAdjudication` to `allowed` on a reviewer or owner ruling, never on a code change.

allowed.text: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar
allowed.reason: Two different intents, no canonical page. `117:235` is the supplication narrated for the specific station between the Yemenite Corner and the Black Stone during tawaf (occasion: hajj-umrah). `quran:2:201` is the ayah itself, indexed as general Qur'anic supplication (occasion: protection). Neither is a duplicate of the other in search intent, and neither is the canonical version of the other — collapsing them would lose a real query for one of the two.
allowed.notes: Not a live collision today: `quran:2:201` has a null transliteration and is `wave_assignment: 1b`, and R3 blocks every `quran:` record from the sitemap until a reviewer-verified clause field exists. `117:235` sits in Wave 1a but no dua detail page is in the sitemap yet (`page-copy.json` `_meta.batches[].approved` is false on both batches). This entry is a forward guard, registered before the collision can occur rather than after.

allowed.text: Allahumma 'alima l-ghaybi wa-sh-shahadah, fatira s-samawati wa-l-ard…
allowed.reason: Two different intents, no canonical page. `27:85` is the supplication placed by its chapter at morning and at evening (occasion: morning-evening, chapter keyword derived per entry); `28:109` is the same wording placed before sleeping (occasion: sleep-waking, chapter keyword "dua for sleeping"). Different chapters, different occasion buckets, different chapter keywords, and separately authored prose that frames each for its own moment. A reader searching what to say before sleeping and a reader searching the morning and evening adhkar are not the same reader, and collapsing them would lose a real query for one of the two.
allowed.notes: Cross-linking is automatic and already built: ADDENDUM §15 emits "The same wording is also listed in this library under …" on each member, filtered to published pages by validator rule R8. No rel=canonical is set on either member, by decision.

allowed.reason: Two different intents, no canonical page. 'Aishah's report attests these words in BOTH postures, and Hisn lists them accordingly: `17:35` under Invocations during Ruku' (keyword "dua for ruku"), `19:43` under Invocations during Sujood (keyword "dua for sujood"). Both chapters carry their own static chapter page. The shared `prayer` occasion bucket is our own facet, not the search intent — "what to say in ruku" and "what to say in sujood" are distinct queries with distinct answers, and a worshipper in one posture is not served by the other page. Authored prose differs throughout and each names its own posture and narrator.

allowed.text: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika mina l-hammi wa-l-hazan…
allowed.reason: Two different intents, no canonical page — the cluster that needed the most scrutiny, since both members sit in the same `distress` occasion bucket. They resolve apart on the evidence: the supplication names eight things, and Hisn lists it under Invocations in times of worry and grief (`34:121`, keyword "dua for worry and grief") AND under Invocations for the settling of a debt (`41:137`, keyword "dua for debt relief") because its own wording covers both — it seeks refuge from anxiety and sorrow AND from the burden of debt and being overpowered by men. "Dua for debt relief" is a distinct query with a distinct need, and the text genuinely answers it. The authored prose on `41:137` states the proportion honestly rather than overclaiming — "Only one of the eight things named concerns debt, and it sits seventh in the list" — so the page serves the debt query without pretending to be a debt-specific supplication. Neither is the canonical version of the other.

pendingAdjudication._note: These 8 clusters were found by the same corpus-wide scan that produced the seed pair. Every one has 2+ SLUGGED members, so each becomes a live R6 failure the moment two of its members are approved for indexing. They are recorded here so the rule's cost is visible in advance — NOT allowed. R6 fails on them until each is adjudicated and moved to `allowed` with a reason, or one member is deindexed. None of them blocks Wave 1a.
pendingAdjudication._seeAlso: DUA-CONTENT-INTEGRITY-v1_0.md §4 A9 #11 — 'Never auto-merge on similarity… Each cluster still needs individual adjudication.' These are that adjudication queue, cited by member id per the same section's convention.

pendingAdjudication.likelyDisposition: REVIEW CAREFULLY — three-member cluster, and the shared text is the single word 'Bismillah'. This is an incidental collision on a very short text rather than a cross-listing of one supplication, which DUA-CONTENT-INTEGRITY-v1_0 §4 names as a distinct cause. Three near-identical pages whose entire dua is one word is a thin-content and cannibalisation risk independent of R6, and may be better served by one page than three.
